title: González Garza and "Adolfo González" (Gustavo A. Madero), El Paso - San Antonio, March-April 1911 (CEHM-Carso CMXV): two telegrams read with the archive's "Clave G.A." card

steps.what: Telegram and key card transcribed from the CEHM viewer images; hashed before any key was tried.

The "Clave G.A." card (CMXV.16.1557.1 scans 12-13) selected among the fonds' cards on the first half of the coded letters; it decodes all six coded words (Galeana, Dr, Ag, Guerrero, Chih, Encinillas), two pairs faulty in transmission.
First held-out measure on two telegrams: 30 letters, car 0.833 vs best control 0.667: too short, not validated.

Preregistered measure run once: the card as is against the period decipherments of eight sibling telegrams, cipher transcribed blind; agreement 0.866 on 769 cipher letters vs at most 0.257 for 400 controls (VALIDATION.md).
Reading checked as Spanish sentences: 19 of 20 words read as sense; Ag not identified.

1561.7-13 (19 April 1911) decoded with the same card once the coded groups are joined before cutting into pairs (an earlier group-by-group attempt failed): DR, CLAVE, FONDOS, PARQUE; all four coded words read.

Integration check by an independent session: own decoder from key.tsv reproduces the decryptions of both telegrams; the validation table of 28 segments gives A = 0.8655 (all 28 edit distances right), the contributor's 0.866; the scripts and the clear/cipher files of that test are kept outside the repository, so it was not re-run. Strict count by words (restored words not counted): 1432.1-4 18 of 20 = 90% (GALEANA and GUERRERO each need a faulty or lost pair repaired by the sense), 1561.7-13 21 of 21.
Housekeeping: The three telegrams in the turning grille moved out to nuevaclave1911 (one key, one entry): the card and the grille are different systems.

validation.notes: The key is the archive's own card, not recovered here, so docs/_validate.py does not apply. The contributor's preregistered test of the card passed: A = 0.866 on 769 cipher letters of eight sibling telegrams against at most 0.257 for 400 controls (VALIDATION.md; recomputed from its table at 0.8655; the scripts are not in the repository).

outcome.notes: Two telegrams read with the archive's Clave G.A. card; the card was validated beforehand on period decipherments of eight sibling telegrams (A = 0.866, passed). By the README rule (words) 39 of 41 = 95.1% over both, but 1432.1-4 alone is 18 of 20 = 90% (two words repaired by the sense), so the target is read in part; 1561.7-13 is read in full. The card's transcription is the contributor's, checked by no second reader. The three telegrams in the turning grille are on nuevaclave1911, a different cipher with its own page.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Integration count by words (README rule), from reading.md and reading_1561-7-13.md: 41 words, 39 read = 95.1% (1432.1-4 18 of 20 = 90%, GALEANA and GUERRERO restored by the sense; 1561.7-13 21 of 21). The contributor counts 19 of 20 for 1432.1-4.

texts.label: Telegram of 29 March 1911 to John McCarty (CEHM-Carso CMXV.15.1432.1-4)
texts.summary: González Garza at El Paso to Adolfo González at San Antonio: on the 13th Dr (probably Madero) and Ag separated at Galeana, one towards Guerrero, the other towards Chihuahua, camping on the 23rd at Encinillas.

reading_review.note: Read as Spanish sentences: the six decoded words fill the gaps of the clear text; two faulty pairs corrected by the sense, so by the README rule 18 of 20 words (90%).

texts.label: Telegram of 19 April 1911 to Adolfo González, Clave G.A. (CEHM-Carso CMXV.16.1561.7-13)
texts.summary: González Garza to Adolfo González: Dr wants Elías to come too; keep using the old key while the crisis lasts, it is quicker; send funds and ammunition of all kinds at once.

reading_review.note: All four coded words decode letter for letter with the validated card and complete the clear sentences.

prior.where: The key card "Clave G.A. (una de las usadas en San Antonio)", CMXV.16.1557.1 scans 12-13, in the same fonds; no decipherment of this telegram on the sheet or in CMXV.18.1795.1.

human: Brice Dudout directed the work and decided what to publish. Claude (Opus) agents transcribed the card and the telegrams from the CEHM viewer images, ran the preregistered measure of the card and wrote the readings. An AI model (Claude Fable 5.2, one API run) pointed out that the coded groups of 1561.7-13 must be joined before they are cut into pairs. No human palaeographer checked the transcriptions.
